description: Progression of strength exercises across guided gym sessions (push_strength_guide / push_workout_guide): load, sets, rest and heart-rate recovery of the same exercise week after week. Each session is read once with the same logic as get_workout_laps, compare_workout_to_plan and get_workout_rest_profile, and the small derived result is cached on disk (~/.suunto-mcp/cache/, SUUNTO_CACHE=off disables it), so repeat calls are cheap. It writes nothing but that cache and never changes anything at Suunto. Looks at the `weeks` weeks (default 8, max 26) ending at `date` (default today; a session that started less than 24 h ago is read but not cached). Reads at most 8 sessions not yet cached per call (two requests each, newest first); the result's `pending` is how many are still unread: CALL AGAIN until pending is 0 before drawing conclusions from the history, unless a note says calling again will not help (cache not writable, sessions failing): then say so instead of looping. A session that fails to load is skipped and listed in `errors`. IMPORTANT: the watch records only the guide's TEXT, so weights and reps are what was PLANNED, not measured; a log_session entry for the session replaces the label's weight with the logged one (loadSource 'journal') and is attached as `journal`. Sessions whose mapping or rest profile is unreliable are included with reliable false and never enter restEndHrMedian. Only the sessions whose heart-rate data is unreliable (dropouts, implausible values, flat-lines, frequent jumps; see get_workout_rest_profile's hrQuality) are also named in a note with the reasons (with name: those with a matching exercise; without: all in the range); a session unreliable for another reason (a missing lap, say) is marked but not named, and one whose FIT has no heart rate at all gets its own note. Without `name`: { from, to, sessions (guided sessions read), exercises: [{ name, sessions, lastDate, lastDetail }] (most sessions first; a name the guide cut to 40 characters is grouped with its longer form only when that is certain: exactly one longer name and at least 12 characters, otherwise they stay separate and a note lists them), pending, errors, notes }. With `name`: { name, from, to, sessions: { cols, rows } (oldest first; cols = date, workoutKey, detail, kg (the first 'NNkg' in the label text, or the top journal set's weight; null when there is none, never guessed), loadSource ('label' | 'journal'), setsDone, plannedSets, restS (the guide's rest), restEndHr / restDropTotal / restT20S / restCoverage (heart-rate recovery of the rest after set 1 from the FIT's record-level HR, null when missing: end-of-rest HR, peak minus end, seconds after the peak to fall 20 bpm, share of the rest's seconds with an HR sample), deviations (compare_workout_to_plan codes for that exercise), reliable, journal), summary: { sessions, firstLoadKg, lastLoadKg, restEndHrMedian (median end-of-rest HR after set 1 over reliable sessions: usable as push_strength_guide's restTargetHr) }, suggestion: { last, target, reason } (the newest session as e.g. '3x8@60kg' or, when set weights differed, '8@60/8@60/5@65kg', and a simple next target: when a log_session entry shows every planned set done with every planned rep at ONE weight, the same sets x reps with a step on top (2.5 kg, but at most 5% of the load in 1.25 kg steps and at least 1.25 kg: 5 kg goes to 6.25); a short set, differing weights between sets (repeat at the lowest weight that reached the reps), a missing load or a rep range written in any way ('3x8-12', '3x8 - 12', '3x8–12', '3x8 to 12') never raise the load: repeat; null without a session; usable as push_strength_guide's per-exercise last/target; nothing is pushed), pending, errors, notes }. `name` is matched ignoring case, accents and punctuation, exactly or, for a name the guide may have cut (12+ characters), as a prefix of the given name. Use the names from the index (or compare_workout_to_plan). Writes only the local cache.

date.description: The last local calendar day of the range, YYYY-MM-DD (default today).

name.description: Exercise name, e.g. 'Back Squat'. Omit for an index of all exercises in the range.

weeks.description: How many weeks the history covers, ending at `date` (default 8).

name: get_exercise_history
title: Get exercise history across sessions
